quick_english: Then, for the suitable adept, the secret rule is stated; then all worship is said to be kula procedure.
Thus, for guru and disciple established in flow, the supreme lord has spoken the essence in ordered worship.
What arises in one month for one appointed to the accomplished order would not arise in a thousand years through various floods of mantras.
Kula of the supreme lord is power, capacity, elevation, freedom, vigor, virility, mass, and consciousness-body.
For one seeing all classes of beings by such nature, with masses of doubt destroyed, worship is indeed of that kind.
For establishing such form, by the path of mind, speech, and body, whatever the hero practices is called kula worship.
Outside, in power, in yamala, in body, in breath path, and in mind: thus kula worship is sixfold, differentiating according to distinction.
Bathing, circle, pot, and the like, or sixfold placement and the like, are not used here; nothing done is for breaking.
Free from six circles, devoid of all coverings, consisting of knower and known: this is declared as kaula in the traishirasa doctrine.
Here in worship, whatever substance is forbidden in scriptural tradition, the wise one should use it immersed in left nectar.
In Shri Brahmayamala it is said: wine is Shiva essence; without it there is no enjoyment or liberation; but with flour, honey, and jaggery it is that.
Female, neuter, and male forms give prior and later enjoyment; but grape-born is supreme radiance, Bhairava free from imagination.
This itself is the pure essence of light, bliss, and consciousness, beloved of the deities and eternal; therefore one should always drink it.
In the glorious Krama secret, by the supreme lord, argha-vessel, sacrifice-abode, and lamp are called three.
The secret in Kaula sacrifice: there argha comes from Shakti union, the abode is named earth-garment-body-seat, and excellence follows in order.
Lamp is ghee-born; cows are indeed remembered as earth-wandering deities; knowing this, the Kaulika should become diligent in those three.
Knowing the primacy of the argha-vessel, doubt may indeed arise about substances stated by Shambhu, and that doubt is defiling.
Having entered the fragrance-rich sacrifice house, facing east or north, one moves from reverse to proper order by supreme impurity.
One should perform purification, burning and nourishing, in order from fierce-gentle distinction, or from mother-presence mantra.
If desiring initiation, plan purification of the path; then, purifying things, by Shakti alone lead them to immortality.
Supreme-enclosure or mother-enclosure mantras, or Mālinī alone, may be used in all rites.
One should fill the argha-vessel with joy-cause-fruit substances, and by the stated mantra identity bring Bhairava selfhood.
By that, the full self, going outside and inner wheel, should be satisfied by drinking drops within upper and lower.
Thus, from the rising full vowel stream union, desiring to see the self outside, one should worship outside.
An auspicious red cloth is set in a sky-like, vermilion-beautiful field.
A coconut-made vessel, filled with wine, appears in an assembled circular form.
The wise should perform sacrifice; the order is said from the northern direction through the northwest to Ganesh.
Worship Vaṭuka, three teachers, Siddhas, and Yoginis, beginning in the east below Ganesh.
The siddha wheel runs through four directions from below Ganesh, with Khagendra and Vijjāmbā.
The tortoise is paired with power and an auspicious girdle-mother.
In the south, the victorious ram is paired with a joyful girdle and Kullāmbā.
Vindhya, conquered by old age, is paired with a girdle, Kuṅkuṇāmbā, and an authoritative six-pair.
In the northwest, Marutta to Īśāna forms the second row, with a sixth in order.
Six powers are named, including Sillā, Eruṇā, Kumārī, Bodhā, and outer-girdle figures.
These authoritative worshipful ones have many differences and an unbroken disciple lineage.
These six seals are named in order, from bliss-line lords to yogi-word figures.
The smaller leftward series runs from thumb to little finger and ends at the root.
The verse lists named billa groups in the rightward series.
The sixfold seats are arranged in order from the named places.
The sign-knower who wanders among seats soon obtains each attainable thing.
These named upward-semen figures are six authority-foot-abandoned ones.
They are called upward-semen because seminal flow is absent in the kula path.
The other guru wives play unafraid with unseized bodies.
There guru-ness is defined as kaula shines in such form.
They are not specially worshipped, only remembered, with air-fire-mother within.
Malini is worshipped in order, then the inner mantra wheel in kula.
In wheel-nature consciousness is mistress, the kula-lady and supreme goddess.
Then she is worshipped as supreme-inferior or single-heroine with kula-lady.
Bhairava, swollen with expanding power, should again worship the pair through the rest of union-bliss.
Like sparks from consciousness of great light form, one should here worship the deity group as a stream of rays.
The inner twelve is to be worshipped, then eight and eight, or four, as desired; what number indeed in the rays?
Maheśi, Vairiñci, Kaumāri, and Vaiṣṇavi are in the four directions; Aindrī, Yāmyā, Muṇḍā, and Yogeshi are in the corners.
The eightfold set from wind-end to aghora is then worshipped in order by the view of union-bliss, becoming paired.
In the eight-eight rite too, in the manifold-named rite, this rite is prescribed in many ways; its number may be a lamp garland.
In the Ratnamala treatise, letter numbers are lamps; the wise should count the letters of the chief worshipped vidya.
One may perform family worship together with pithas, fields, and so on, as spoken by the supreme lord in the Madhava family.
The fourfold set named creation, preservation, destruction, and order, together with pithas and cremation grounds, should be worshipped for enjoyment and liberation.
One should remember this rite for self or for Shakti's wheel, placing it in the body called pitha, supreme-lordly.
Attahasam is at the crown place, Caritra in the ear hole, Kaulagiri in the ears, and Jayantika in the nostril holes.
Ujjayini is at the brows, Prayaga in the mouth, Varanasi in the heart, Shripitha at the shoulder pair, and Viraja in the throat.

quick_english: These five lakshas declared — perform tenth-part homa; in eyes, in going-coming, in mouth, in hamsa, and in aksa-rosary.
In the union of Shiva and Shakti, six hundred thousand recitations are said to apply to the eyes, going and coming, ear, hamsa, and mouth, O fair one.
Recitation is remembered as sevenfold in the hand, pair, eyes, going and coming, ear and mouth, secret, and secret place.
This recitation, middle-placed in hundred-spoked and thousand-spoked centers, O fair one, is one hundred thousand of Rudra, and offering here is by one tenth.
In the eyes, going and coming, ears, mouth, between the brahma opening, breasts, hands, feet, and secret wheel, one should practice twice.
Wherever the eye goes, wherever the mind goes, there the hamsa is to be practiced twice, being of expansion and contraction nature.
That self is Matrika, the goddess, Shiva situated in the body; therefore one should not practice the distinction 'that other is I'.
For one who distinguishes, accomplishment and liberation are far away; then, as previously said, in the sixteen-hundred-thousand and so on breath course.
Abandonment of pure and impure distinctions is called single-pointed; standing there, this very self offers and also recites.
Recitation is chattering activity of sound-reflection essence; dissolution of that rubbed essence in the fire of consciousness is proclaimed as offering.
Reflection was declared before as the twelvefold goddess essence; there, the offering act of dissolution form involves the two final knowledges.
Thus ten others in offering, one tenth, O Shri Shambhunatha, first kshatriya meaning ocean moon.
When this one worships together with the externally standing power, then this secret rule declared by the supreme lord is spoken.

quick_english: By pride-firmness-binding sequence, consciousness-named piercing — in heart-space immediately bears divine-knowledge-sun rising.
The body is supreme in subtle essence and gross in shadow form; it is known facing or turned away from mirror-like supports.
Thus one pacifies body divisions swiftly and gradually through channels, reaching supreme state by body piercing.
Whatever wheel is in the body, going to infant rest, gradually brightens that wheel; piercing gives named place and fruit.
Channels are three principal and others innumerable; unification by them is channel piercing here, making fruit.
In channel piercing, desired channel flow with principal endings like eye gives varied knowledge attainment.
The great yogi, by force, bursts the other channel enclosed by the strong tail-shaped channel and casts it down on earth.
Touching nonduality in all wheels through supreme piercing, the teacher should make supreme Shiva, giving Shiva state.
Thus determined in the Shri Viravali lineage: the indivisible middle is to be known in every way; knowing it, one is not stained.
In that division order, the accomplished teacher liberates bound beings; the disciple enters before the teacher, and mouth pierces mouth.
Form in form unifies with objects; when mind becomes unified, the two attain a beyond-mind state.
By mind movement of both, at that time one becomes initiated; in moon-sun union the living being goes to that identity.
Here gods from Brahma, desiring liberation, restrain their own ray wheel for both enjoyment and liberation.
If that initiation is proclaimed as Shiva's, this motionless liberation is told for all beings.
From the striking union of fire and moon parts, pulsation removes external breath gone outward through darkness-form union.
Gone out through hair pores, wandering with all causes, taking the unmarked middle, it makes wander and releases.
By union and uprooting method, pierce the five knots; contemplate the union activity pair in the middle abode.
One should not join self, space, outside, mantra, and body; this initiation gives Shiva state to all beings.
At initiation end, having cooked lamps, the offering should be eaten with all adepts by clan teachers destroying great sin.
Thus in Shri Ratnamala, the extra rite indeed pacifies that sin, and this pacification is proclaimed.
Next day the teacher's sacrifice should be done by him, because without it the rite does not reach completeness; do that with effort then.
By which the teacher is pleased, that should be offered to him; in the circle rite interval, movement is called the rite.
Having seen the well-filled bee vessel placed in the hero lord's hand, supreme Brahman, that should be drunk by the teacher's command.
Having satisfied beings, one should offer to the teacher; having made the teacher on earth, bowed and taken, satisfying sky-goers.
Having saluted own mantra, and that, female messenger, Ganapati, teachers, field protector, hero group, then by teacher order.
The substance touched by the hero should be drunk by oneself, never otherwise; those who know supreme Brahman are free from coming and going.
This should not be done together with those possessed of greed, delusion, pride, anger, attachment, and deceit, by one seeking welfare for oneself.
At the beginning, middle, and end of sacrifice, in guru worship, and in prescribed occasional rites, the disciple should perform this rite.
Thus the secret rite has been discussed and is very clear from the guru's mouth-experience.
